khon-ninh-cung: A brand-new painting of a natural, lived-in, richly furnished room, painted exactly like image 1 (the bedroom): same hand, same brushwork, same soft painterly finish, same natural warm colours, saturation and contrast, same depth with furniture, curtains and objects arranged through the whole room from the foreground to the back. Wide panoramic, eye-level view, summer morning. ROOM: Khôn Ninh cung reception hall, where the Empress of an ancient Chinese imperial palace receives the consorts, a real room in daily use, no bed anywhere: red lacquer pillars with gilded phoenix carving, golden lattice windows at the back onto a sunny summer garden; on a low dais a carved gilded throne seat (a wide Chinese throne with a tall carved panel back) with imperial yellow silk cushions embroidered with phoenixes and a small low table with a gold tea set, behind it a large gilded folding screen with a phoenix among peonies, a pair of golden phoenix figures on tall stands; below the dais, rows of paired Chinese armchairs with small tea tables between them for the visiting consorts; NO table and NO stools in the middle of the floor (owner Lượt 554): the floor in the middle in front of the dais stays open for people to stand; the small tea tables stand only between the armchairs along the sides, each table beside its seats, and a tall gilt incense stand and potted peonies stand only at the sides beside the dais; imperial yellow sheer curtains tied back with gold tassels, ornate gilded palace lanterns, side tables with cloisonné and porcelain vases of peonies, curio shelves of jade and gold treasures. The most dazzling room of the whole palace: imperial yellow silk and gold everywhere, phoenix motifs carved, embroidered and gilded, red lacquer pillars wrapped with gold, the richest treasures. No Western sofa, no upholstered couch. The bottom-right corner nearest the viewer stays almost clear, holding at most one small object; tea tables and stools stand further back in the room. FLOOR SHARE (owner Lượt 520): Keep the same room and the same arrangement as image 3 (this same room as drawn before), except that the low table and stools in the middle of its floor are removed, seen a little closer and lower so less floor shows: the furniture comes down to about seven eighths of the picture height, and the open floor in front is only a strip of about one tenth of the picture height at the centre, clearly less floor than in image 3. FLOOR: polished stone tiles visible between the furniture, no large rug or carpet covering the floor (at most a small mat at the foot of the dais); the throne seat on its dais sits in the central half of the width. LIGHT: soft warm morning daylight from the right, like the light on the girl in image 2, so a person standing in the room looks lit by it. Do not leave the room empty like a stage; it should feel natural and furnished, people will simply be placed in it later. LEFT SIDE (owner Lượt 406): the left part of the room near the viewer stays open like in image 1 — only small, low objects there at most, never a large piece of furniture or a big object close up at the left edge, because people will stand on the left. Empty of people, no text.
